title: Why Your Passenger Mirror Lies to You
hook: Never trust your passenger mirror's distance.

script.narration: Never trust your passenger mirror's distance.
script.visual_search: car side mirror highway traffic fast

script.narration: Your driver's side mirror is flat, so cars look their true size. Since the passenger mirror sits farther away, flat glass would leave a huge blind spot.
script.visual_search: driver checking car side mirror close up

script.narration: To fix that, automakers curve the passenger glass outward. This convex shape widens your view, but shrinks cars so they look farther away than they really are.

description:
Have you noticed the warning printed on your passenger side mirror? It is there because the two side mirrors on your car are actually shaped differently for safety.

In this 60-second driving tip, learn why automakers use a convex mirror on the passenger side, how it eliminates blind spots, and why it makes approaching cars look smaller and farther away.

Follow Learn in 60 Seconds for quick, practical driving tips and everyday car facts.
why_it_will_work: Viewers on this channel consistently watch practical car-feature explanations like the fuel gauge arrow and blinking turn signals, and this pairs a strong curiosity hook with high-volume beginner driving search terms.
quality_problems: fact-check: Claiming the driver's side mirror is flat is only true in some regions (like North America), as convex or aspheric driver's side mirrors are common in Europe and other parts of the world.; Saying 'Never trust your passenger mirror's distance' and that it 'lies to you' is exaggerated, since it still shows relative distance and includes a warning label where required.
